## 1. Setup

```{r}
#| label: setup

library(readxl)
library(dplyr)
library(ggplot2)
library(sf)
library(rnaturalearthdata)
library(patchwork)
library(metafor)

# Use the thesis project's output folder for all figures and model summaries.
dir.create("outputs", showWarnings = FALSE)
```

## 2. Data Import

```{r}
#| label: data-import
# Read study information, experimental arm information and treatment-control response records.
file_path <- "../03_Extraction_Data/data table - thesis.xlsx"


file.exists(file_path)


excel_sheets(file_path)

# Keep the three worksheets at their study, experimental-arm and response-comparison levels.
study_info <- read_excel(file_path, sheet = "Study_information")
experiment_info <- read_excel(file_path, sheet = "Experiment_information")
effect_size_data <- read_excel(file_path, sheet = "Effect_size_data")


dim(study_info)
dim(experiment_info)
dim(effect_size_data)
```

## 3. Descriptive Analysis

### Figure 1 — Study selection process

This R code covers only the data analyses and related figure and table outputs, so it does not include the study selection flowchart (Figure 1). To make the outputs easy to match to the thesis and avoid confusion, figure numbering follows the thesis, starting from Figure 2.

### Figure 2 — Geographical and temporal distribution of studies

```{r}
#| label: figure2-distribution-data

# 1. Prepare study-level data --------------------------------------------------
names(study_info) <- trimws(names(study_info))

study_data <- study_info |>
  transmute(
    Study_ID = trimws(as.character(`Study ID`)),
    Year = as.numeric(Year),
    Location = trimws(`Experiment location`),
    Longitude = as.numeric(Longitude),
    Latitude = as.numeric(Latitude),
    Ecosystem = na_if(trimws(Ecosystem), ""),
    Setting = na_if(trimws(Setting), ""),
    Scale = na_if(trimws(`Experimental Scale`), "")
  ) |>
  distinct()

# Remove identical study records. Stop counting if information conflicts within Study_ID.

if (anyNA(study_data$Study_ID) ||
    any(study_data$Study_ID == "") ||
    anyDuplicated(study_data$Study_ID) > 0L) {
  stop("Study ID is missing or has conflicting information. Check study_data.")
}

# Check years and coordinates so records with missing values are not silently omitted from plots.
data_issues <- study_data |>
  filter(
    !is.finite(Year) | Year != floor(Year) |
    !is.finite(Longitude) | !is.finite(Latitude) |
    abs(Longitude) > 180 | abs(Latitude) > 90
  )

if (nrow(data_issues) > 0L) {
  print(data_issues)
  stop("The years or coordinates in the records above need manual review.")
}


# 2. Count independent studies by publication year --------------------------------------
# Each row of study_data is a unique Study ID, so each study is counted once.
year_counts <- study_data |>
  count(Year, name = "Number_of_studies")

# Include every year from the earliest to the latest publication year.
# Set years with no studies to 0 so the line does not skip them.
year_counts <- data.frame(
  Year = seq(min(study_data$Year), max(study_data$Year))
) |>
  left_join(year_counts, by = "Year") |>
  mutate(
    Number_of_studies = coalesce(Number_of_studies, 0L)
  )

# Print annual study counts.
print(year_counts)


# 3. Count studies at each coordinate ---------------------------------------------
# Combine records only when longitude and latitude are identical. Do not combine nearby locations with different coordinates.
# Count unique Study IDs. This summary is used only for the map and does not change study_data.
location_counts <- study_data |>
  group_by(Longitude, Latitude) |>
  summarise(
    Number_of_studies = n_distinct(Study_ID),
    .groups = "drop"
  )

# Map symbols represent 1–5 studies per coordinate. Counts outside this range trigger a check.
if (any(location_counts$Number_of_studies > 5L)) {
  stop("A coordinate has more than 5 studies. Add the corresponding colour and shape.")
}

# Treat counts as categories so both colour and shape can represent them.
location_counts <- location_counts |>
  mutate(Study_count = factor(Number_of_studies, levels = 1:5))

# Print the number of independent studies at each coordinate.
print(location_counts)

world_map <- rnaturalearthdata::countries50
```

```{r}
#| label: fig-figure2a-geographical-distribution
#| fig-width: 6.3
#| fig-height: 3.8
#| fig-align: center
#| dpi: 300

# 4. Geographical panel: study locations and study counts ---------------------------------
# Draw one symbol per coordinate. Colour and shape both show the number of studies at that location.
figure2a <- ggplot() +
  geom_sf(
    data = world_map,
    fill = "#333333",
    colour = "#606060",
    linewidth = 0.10
  ) +
  geom_point(
    data = location_counts,
    aes(
      x = Longitude,
      y = Latitude,
      colour = Study_count,
      shape = Study_count
    ),
    size = 3.2,
    stroke = 1
  ) +
  scale_colour_manual(
    name = "Number of studies",
    values = c(
      "1" = "#FF8C85",  
      "2" = "#2CA25F",  
      "3" = "#9467BD",  
      "4" = "#377EB8",  
      "5" = "#E69F00"   
    )
  ) +
  scale_shape_manual(
  name = "Number of studies",
  values = c(
    "1" = "●",  
    "2" = "▲",  
    "3" = "■",  
    "4" = "★",  
    "5" = "◆"   
  )
  ) +
  coord_sf(
    crs = "+proj=robin",
    default_crs = st_crs(4326),
    datum = NA,
    expand = FALSE
  ) +
  labs(title = "a  Geographical distribution") +
  theme_void(base_size = 11, base_family = "sans") +
  theme(
    panel.background = element_rect(fill = "#ECECEC", colour = NA),
    plot.background = element_rect(fill = "white", colour = NA),
    plot.title = element_text(size = 12, face = "bold", hjust = 0.5,
      margin = margin(b = 5)),
    legend.position = "bottom",
    legend.direction = "horizontal",
    legend.title = element_text(size = 11),
    legend.text = element_text(size = 11),
    legend.key.size = grid::unit(5, "mm"),
    legend.spacing.x = grid::unit(2, "pt"),
    legend.margin = margin(1, 0, 0, 0),
    legend.box.margin = margin(0, 0, 0, 0),
    plot.margin = margin(4, 4, 3, 4)
  ) +
  guides(colour = guide_legend(nrow = 1, title.position = "left",
    override.aes = list(size = 4.2)))

print(figure2a)
```

### Figure 3 — Ecosystems and experimental settings

```{r}
#| label: fig-figure3
#| fig-width: 7.2
#| fig-height: 5.6
#| fig-align: center
#| dpi: 600

# Prepare study-level categories for ecosystem, experimental setting and experimental scale.


figure3_data <- study_info |>
  transmute(
    Study_ID = `Study ID`,
    Ecosystem = Ecosystem,
    Setting = Setting,
    Scale = `Experimental Scale`
  )

# 1. Check ecosystem, setting and scale categories ----------------------------------
classification_issues <- figure3_data |>
  filter(
    !(Ecosystem %in% c("Stream", "River", "Lake", "Wetland", "Other")) |
    !(Setting %in% c("Lab", "Outdoor")) |
    !(Scale %in% c("Microcosm", "Mesocosm"))
  )

# Print records with categories outside the expected values and stop plotting.
if (nrow(classification_issues) > 0) {
  print(classification_issues)
  stop("Some categories have not been standardised. Re-import the latest Excel data.")
}

# 2. Summarise ecosystems and experimental scales ---------------------------------------------
# The shared data have been checked for unique Study IDs, so each study is counted once.
ecosystem_counts <- figure3_data |>
  count(Ecosystem, Scale, name = "Number_of_studies") |>
  mutate(
    Scale = factor(Scale, levels = c("Microcosm", "Mesocosm"))
  )

# Calculate the total for each ecosystem to order the bars and label their ends.
ecosystem_totals <- ecosystem_counts |>
  group_by(Ecosystem) |>
  summarise(
    Number_of_studies = sum(Number_of_studies),
    .groups = "drop"
  ) |>
  arrange(desc(Number_of_studies), Ecosystem)


# 3. Summarise experimental settings -------------------------------------------------------
# Use all included studies as the percentage denominator. Keep unrounded percentages for plotting.
setting_counts <- figure3_data |>
  count(Setting, name = "Number_of_studies") |>
  mutate(
    Setting = factor(Setting, levels = c("Lab", "Outdoor"))
  ) |>
  arrange(Setting) |>
  mutate(
    Percentage = 100 * Number_of_studies / sum(Number_of_studies),
    xmax = 100 * cumsum(Number_of_studies) / sum(Number_of_studies),
    xmin = xmax - Percentage,

    # Labels show the name, count and percentage. Round percentages to one decimal place in labels only.
    Label = sprintf(
      "%s · %d (%.1f%%)",
      Setting, Number_of_studies, Percentage
    ),

    # Place the Lab label on the left and the Outdoor label on the right to avoid crowding the smaller section.
    Label_x = if_else(Setting == "Lab", 0, 100),
    Label_hjust = if_else(Setting == "Lab", 0, 1)
  )

# Print ecosystem-by-scale counts and experimental-setting proportions.
print(ecosystem_counts)
print(setting_counts)


# 4. Set shared titles and spacing for the two plots -----------------------------------------
figure3_theme <- theme(
  plot.title = element_text(size = 12, face = "bold", hjust = 0.5),
  plot.background = element_rect(fill = "white", colour = NA),
  plot.margin = margin(8, 12, 8, 10)
)


# 5. Figure 3a: ecosystems and experimental scales --------------------------------------
# Use one horizontal stacked bar for each ecosystem.
# Blue-green represents Microcosm and orange represents Mesocosm. Label each bar end with its total study count.
figure3a <- ggplot(
  ecosystem_counts,
  aes(x = Number_of_studies, y = Ecosystem, fill = Scale)
) +
  geom_col(
    width = 0.65,
    position = position_stack(reverse = TRUE)
  ) +
  geom_text(
    data = ecosystem_totals,
    aes(
      x = Number_of_studies,
      y = Ecosystem,
      label = Number_of_studies
    ),
    inherit.aes = FALSE,
    hjust = -0.35,
    size = 3.5
  ) +
  scale_y_discrete(
    limits = rev(ecosystem_totals$Ecosystem)
  ) +
  scale_x_continuous(
    breaks = seq(0, max(ecosystem_totals$Number_of_studies)),
    expand = expansion(mult = c(0, 0.10))
  ) +
  scale_fill_manual(
    name = "Experimental scale",
    values = c(
      "Microcosm" = "#377F89",
      "Mesocosm" = "#EBA05A"
    )
  ) +
  labs(
    title = "a  Ecosystem types and experimental scale",
    x = "Number of studies",
    y = "Ecosystem type"
  ) +
  theme_classic(base_size = 11) +
  figure3_theme +
  theme(
    panel.grid.major.x = element_line(colour = "#E9E9E9", linewidth = 0.3),
    legend.position = "bottom",
    legend.title = element_text(size = 10),
    legend.text = element_text(size = 10)
  )


# 6. Figure 3b: percentage bar for experimental settings ------------------------------------

# Place labels above the percentage bar so low-frequency categories remain readable.
figure3b <- ggplot(setting_counts) +
  geom_rect(
    aes(xmin = xmin, xmax = xmax, fill = Setting),
    ymin = 0,
    ymax = 0.28
  ) +
  geom_text(
    aes(
      x = Label_x,
      label = Label,
      hjust = Label_hjust
    ),
    y = 0.50,
    size = 3.5
  ) +
  scale_fill_manual(
    values = c(
      "Lab" = "#377F89",
      "Outdoor" = "#EBA05A"
    )
  ) +
  scale_x_continuous(
    limits = c(0, 100),
    breaks = c(0, 100),
    labels = c("0%", "100%"),
    expand = c(0, 0)
  ) +
  scale_y_continuous(
    limits = c(-0.12, 0.75),
    expand = c(0, 0)
  ) +
  labs(title = "b  Experimental settings") +
  theme_void(base_size = 11) +
  figure3_theme +
  theme(
    axis.text.x = element_text(size = 10, colour = "#555555"),
    legend.position = "none"
  )


# 7. Stack the plots vertically and save -----------------------------------------------------
figure3 <- wrap_plots(
  figure3a,
  figure3b,
  ncol = 1,
  heights = c(3, 1)
)

print(figure3)

# Export a vector PDF and a PNG with dimensions matching the code chunk settings.
ggsave(
  "outputs/Figure3_Ecosystems_experimental_settings.pdf", plot = figure3,
  width = 7.2, height = 5.6, units = "in", bg = "white"
)

ggsave(
  "outputs/Figure3_Ecosystems_experimental_settings.png", plot = figure3,
  width = 7.2, height = 5.6, units = "in",
  dpi = 600, bg = "white"
)
```

### Figure 4 — Polymer type, particle size and particle shape

```{r}
#| label: fig-figure4-layout
#| fig-width: 12
#| fig-height: 3.5
#| out-width: 100%
#| fig-align: center
#| dpi: 600

# Figure 4: polymer type, particle size and particle shape -------------------------------------
# Use the experimental-arm table experiment_info as input.




# 1. Select plastic-exposure treatment arms -------------------------------------------------
# Use both Arm_ID and Polymer_design:
# Exclude controls and arms exposed only to a co-contaminant without plastic.
# Prepare plastic treatment arms in plastic_data and keep the original fields.
plastic_data <- experiment_info |>
  mutate(
    across(
      c(Study_ID, Arm_ID, Polymer_design),
      ~ trimws(as.character(.x))
    )
  ) |>
  filter(
    Study_ID %in% study_data$Study_ID,
    grepl("_T[0-9]+$", Arm_ID),
    Polymer_design == "Single"
  )


# 2. Standardise polymer types and shapes ---------------------------------------------
# Standardise polymer names in a separate column and retain original names for traceability.
# Combine shape synonyms using the explicit mappings below.
plastic_data <- plastic_data |>
  mutate(
    polymer_key = toupper(trimws(as.character(Polymer_type))),
    shape_key = tolower(trimws(as.character(Polymer_shape))),

    Polymer_type_clean = case_when(
      polymer_key %in% c("PS", "PE", "PP", "PVC", "PET", "PLA", "TWP") ~
        polymer_key,
      polymer_key == "AF RESIN" ~ "AF resin",
      polymer_key == "OTHER" ~ "Other",
      is.na(polymer_key) | polymer_key %in% c("", "NA", "NR", "NONE") ~
        "Not reported",
      TRUE ~ NA_character_
    ),

    Polymer_shape_clean = case_when(
      shape_key %in% c("microsphere", "microbead", "sphere") ~ "Sphere/bead",
      shape_key %in% c("irregular", "irregular particle") ~ "Irregular",
      shape_key == "microfiber" ~ "Fiber",
      shape_key == "fragment" ~ "Fragment",
      shape_key == "granule" ~ "Granule",
      shape_key == "raspberry-like" ~
        "Raspberry-like",
      shape_key == "particle" ~
        "Particle",
      is.na(shape_key) | shape_key %in% c("", "na", "nr", "none") ~
        "Not reported",
      TRUE ~ NA_character_
    )
  )


# 3. Classify particle sizes into intervals (μm) --------------------------------------------
# Use Particle_size_μm. Its units are already harmonised, so no further conversion from nm or mm is needed.
# Classify single values directly. Use the mapping table for ranges, not their midpoints.
# Classify ranges spanning several intervals as Other.
size_levels <- c(
  "<1", "1-<100", "100-<200", "200-<500",
  "500-<1000", "1000-5000", "Other", "Not reported"
)

size_range_map <- c(
  "0.05-0.10" = "<1",
  "<=0.1" = "<1",
  "10-45" = "1-<100",
  "8-20" = "1-<100",
  "1-4" = "1-<100",
  "63-75" = "1-<100",
  "1-5" = "1-<100",
  "62-149" = "Other",
  ">0.1-5000" = "Other"
)

plastic_data <- plastic_data |>
  mutate(
    # Standardise range symbols and remove spaces for matching.
    Size_text = gsub(
      "[[:space:]]+", "", as.character(`Particle_size_μm`)
    ),
    Size_text = gsub("[–—−]", "-", Size_text),
    Size_text = sub("^≤", "<=", Size_text),

    # Convert only single values to numeric. Handle ranges with the mapping table.
    Size_value = as.numeric(
      if_else(
        grepl("^[0-9]+(\\.[0-9]+)?$", Size_text),
        Size_text,
        NA_character_
      )
    ),

    Particle_size_clean = case_when(
      is.na(Size_text) | toupper(Size_text) %in% c("", "NA", "NR", "NONE") ~
        "Not reported",

      Size_text %in% names(size_range_map) ~
        unname(size_range_map[Size_text]),

      Size_value > 0 & Size_value <= 5000 ~
        as.character(cut(
          Size_value,
          breaks = c(0, 1, 100, 200, 500, 1000, Inf),
          labels = size_levels[1:6],
          right = FALSE
        )),

      TRUE ~ NA_character_
    ),

    Particle_size_clean = factor(
      Particle_size_clean,
      levels = size_levels
    )
  )

# List unmatched particle sizes as issues and stop further classification and counting.
unmatched <- plastic_data |>
  filter(
    is.na(Polymer_type_clean) |
    is.na(Polymer_shape_clean) |
    is.na(Particle_size_clean)
  ) |>
  distinct(Study_ID, Polymer_type, Polymer_shape, `Particle_size_μm`)

if (nrow(unmatched) > 0L) {
  print(unmatched, n = Inf)
  stop("Some categories or particle sizes are not recognised. Check the table above and confirm that the latest Excel data have been imported.")
}


# 4. Remove duplicates and count study-category combinations separately --------------------------------
# Different concentrations, exposure times and experimental groups in one study do not increase its count within the same category.
# A study covering several categories can be counted once in each category.
polymer_counts <- plastic_data |>
  distinct(Study_ID, Polymer_type_clean) |>
  count(Polymer_type_clean, name = "Number_of_studies", sort = TRUE)

size_counts <- plastic_data |>
  distinct(Study_ID, Particle_size_clean) |>
  count(Particle_size_clean, name = "Number_of_studies")

shape_counts <- plastic_data |>
  distinct(Study_ID, Polymer_shape_clean) |>
  count(Polymer_shape_clean, name = "Number_of_studies", sort = TRUE)

# Print polymer and shape mappings, particle-size categories and study counts.
polymer_mapping <- plastic_data |>
  distinct(Polymer_type, Polymer_type_clean) |>
  arrange(Polymer_type_clean)

size_mapping <- plastic_data |>
  distinct(`Particle_size_μm`, Particle_size_clean) |>
  arrange(Particle_size_clean)

print(polymer_mapping, n = Inf)
print(size_mapping, n = Inf)
print(polymer_counts, n = Inf)
print(size_counts, n = Inf)
print(shape_counts, n = Inf)


# 5. Set colours -----------------------------------------------------------
# The three pie charts use study-category counts for polymer type, particle size and shape, respectively.

pie_palette <- c(
  "#A6CEE3", "#1F78B4", "#B2DF8A", "#33A02C",
  "#FB9A99", "#E31A1C", "#FDBF6F", "#FF7F00",
  "#CAB2D6", "#6A3D9A"
)


# 6. Create a pie chart on the left and a legend on the right -----------------------------------------
# Use the same space proportions for all three panels so the pies have the same size.
# Place category titles above the legends and a/b/c separately at the upper left of each pie.
make_pie_panel <- function(count_data, category, legend_title, tag) {

  plot_data <- count_data |>
    transmute(
      Category = as.character(.data[[category]]),
      Number_of_studies
    )

  plot_data$Category <- factor(
    plot_data$Category,
    levels = plot_data$Category
  )

  fill_colours <- setNames(
    pie_palette[seq_len(nrow(plot_data))],
    levels(plot_data$Category)
  )
  fill_colours[names(fill_colours) == "Other"] <- "#BDBDBD"
  fill_colours[names(fill_colours) == "Not reported"] <- "#E5E5E5"

  pie <- ggplot(
    plot_data,
    aes(x = "", y = Number_of_studies, fill = Category)
  ) +
    geom_col(
      width = 1,
      colour = "#222222",
      linewidth = 0.3,
      position = position_stack(reverse = TRUE)
    ) +
    coord_polar(theta = "y") +
    scale_y_continuous(expand = c(0, 0)) +
    scale_fill_manual(
      name = legend_title,
      values = fill_colours,
      breaks = levels(plot_data$Category),
      labels = scales::label_wrap(18)
    ) +
    labs(tag = tag) +
    guides(fill = guide_legend(ncol = 1)) +
    theme_void(base_size = 12) +
    theme(
      plot.tag = element_text(size = 16, face = "bold"),
      plot.tag.position = c(0.04, 0.98),
      plot.margin = margin(8, 0, 8, 4),
      legend.position = "right",
      legend.direction = "vertical",
      legend.title = element_text(size = 12, face = "bold"),
      legend.text = element_text(size = 11),
      legend.key.size = grid::unit(3.5, "mm"),
      legend.margin = margin(0, 0, 0, 0),
      legend.box.margin = margin(0, 0, 0, 0)
    )

  # Place the legend in a separate area on the right so it does not reduce the pie's space.
  wrap_plots(
    pie,
    guide_area(),
    nrow = 1,
    widths = c(1.3, 1),
    guides = "collect"
  )
}

figure4a <- make_pie_panel(
  polymer_counts, "Polymer_type_clean", "Polymer type", "a"
)

figure4b <- make_pie_panel(
  size_counts, "Particle_size_clean", "Particle size (µm)", "b"
)

figure4c <- make_pie_panel(
  shape_counts, "Polymer_shape_clean", "Particle shape", "c"
)


# 7. Arrange panels horizontally and save -----------------------------------------------------
# Wrap each panel separately to retain its internal pie-and-legend layout.
figure4 <- wrap_plots(
  wrap_elements(full = figure4a),
  wrap_elements(full = figure4b),
  wrap_elements(full = figure4c),
  nrow = 1,
  widths = c(1, 1, 1)
) +
  plot_annotation(
    caption = paste(
      "Counts represent unique study-category combinations;",
      "a study may contribute to multiple categories."
    ),
    theme = theme(
      plot.caption = element_text(size = 10, hjust = 0),
      plot.background = element_rect(fill = "white", colour = NA),
      plot.margin = margin(4, 6, 4, 6)
    )
  )

print(figure4)

# Export the three horizontally arranged pie charts and their legends.
ggsave(
  "outputs/Figure4_Plastic_characteristics.pdf", plot = figure4,
  width = 12, height = 3.5, units = "in", bg = "white"
)

ggsave(
  "outputs/Figure4_Plastic_characteristics.png", plot = figure4,
  width = 12, height = 3.5, units = "in",
  dpi = 600, bg = "white"
)
```

### Figure 5 — Exposure concentration and duration

```{r}
#| label: figure5-refresh-data
# Read arm-level exposure information from Experiment_information.
# The dual-axis scatter plot uses harmonised units and deduplicated exposure conditions.

library(dplyr)
library(ggplot2)
experiment_info <- readxl::read_excel(
  "../03_Extraction_Data/data table - thesis.xlsx",
  sheet = "Experiment_information", range = readxl::cell_cols("A:Q")
)
```

```{r}
#| label: figure5-exposure-conditions
# Figure 5: explore exposure concentration × exposure duration -------------------------------
# Prepare concentration, units, duration and exclusion reasons in a separate data object.



# 1. Standardise units and record exclusion reasons -----------------------------------------
exposure_data <- experiment_info |>
  mutate(
    across(
      c(Study_ID, Experiment_ID, Polymer_design),
      ~ trimws(as.character(.x))
    ),

    # Convert values that cannot be parsed to NA and include them in the review table below.
    Concentration_numeric = suppressWarnings(
      as.numeric(as.character(Concentration_value))
    ),
    Duration_days = suppressWarnings(
      as.numeric(as.character(Duration_Day))
    ),

    # Replace both microgram symbols with u and remove spaces from units.
    Unit_clean = tolower(gsub(
      "[[:space:]]+", "",
      chartr("µμ", "uu", as.character(Concentration_unit))
    )),

    Concentration_type = case_when(
      Unit_clean %in% c("mg/l", "ug/l", "ug/ml") ~ "Mass",
      Unit_clean %in% c("particles/l", "particles/ml", "fibers/l") ~ "Count",
      TRUE ~ NA_character_
    ),

    # Convert mass concentrations to mg/L and number concentrations to particles/L.
    # 1 µg/mL = 1 mg/L. Keep fibers/L values unchanged and record their source separately.
    Concentration_std = case_when(
      Unit_clean == "ug/l" ~ Concentration_numeric / 1000,
      Unit_clean == "particles/ml" ~ Concentration_numeric * 1000,
      Unit_clean %in% c("mg/l", "ug/ml", "particles/l", "fibers/l") ~
        Concentration_numeric,
      TRUE ~ NA_real_
    ),

    # Record the first exclusion reason for each row.
    # Select plastic exposures with Polymer_design = Single.
    Exclusion_reason = case_when(
      grepl("silica", Unit_clean, fixed = TRUE) ~ "Non-plastic particles: silica",
      !is.finite(Concentration_numeric) ~ "Concentration is missing or cannot be parsed",
      Concentration_numeric == 0 ~ "Concentration is 0",
      Concentration_numeric < 0 ~ "Negative concentration",
      is.na(Polymer_design) | Polymer_design != "Single" ~
        "Not marked as plastic exposure",
      is.na(Concentration_type) ~ "Concentration unit is not supported for conversion",
      !is.finite(Concentration_std) ~ "Standardised concentration is not finite",
      !is.finite(Duration_days) | Duration_days <= 0 ~
        "Exposure duration is missing, cannot be parsed or is not positive",
      is.na(Study_ID) | Study_ID == "" |
        is.na(Experiment_ID) | Experiment_ID == "" ~
        "Missing study or experiment ID",
      TRUE ~ NA_character_
    )
  )

# Retain original concentrations, units and durations so excluded records can be checked.
excluded_records <- exposure_data |>
  filter(!is.na(Exclusion_reason)) |>
  select(
    Study_ID, Experiment_ID, Arm_ID,
    Concentration_value, Concentration_unit, Duration_Day,
    Exclusion_reason
  ) |>
  distinct()


# 2. Remove duplicate exposure conditions -----------------------------------------------------
# Keep different concentration levels and durations.
# Identify exposure conditions by study, experiment, concentration type, standardised concentration and duration.
# Differences in polymer, particle size or co-exposure under the same key do not count as separate exposure conditions.

exposure_conditions <- exposure_data |>
  filter(is.na(Exclusion_reason)) |>
  group_by(
    Concentration_type, Study_ID, Experiment_ID,
    Concentration_std, Duration_days
  ) |>
  summarise(
    Source_units = paste(
      sort(unique(as.character(Concentration_unit))),
      collapse = "; "
    ),
    Includes_fibers = any(Unit_clean == "fibers/l"),
    .groups = "drop"
  ) |>
  mutate(
    Standard_unit = if_else(
      Concentration_type == "Mass", "mg/L", "particles/L"
    ),

    # Keep fractional days, such as 0.125 day. Do not round duration to whole days.
    Duration_bin = cut(
      Duration_days,
      breaks = c(0, 7, 14, 30, 60, Inf),
      labels = c("≤7", ">7–14", ">14–30", ">30–60", ">60"),
      right = TRUE
    )
  )


# Separate concentration measurement types to set the two axis ranges. Do not convert between units.
mass_conditions <- exposure_conditions |> filter(Concentration_type == "Mass")
count_conditions <- exposure_conditions |> filter(Concentration_type == "Count")
print(excluded_records)
```

```{r}
#| label: figure5-scatter
#| fig-width: 6.3
#| fig-height: 5.5

# 1. Prepare individual exposure conditions for the scatter plot --------------------------------------
# Each row is one defined Study_ID + Experiment_ID + concentration type + concentration + duration combination.
# Keep Source_units and Includes_fibers. Show the two concentration types in their respective original units.
print(
  exposure_conditions |>
    group_by(Concentration_type) |>
    summarise(Exposure_conditions = n(), Studies = n_distinct(Study_ID), .groups = "drop")
)

# 2. Set a mapping in log10 space for display only --------------------------------
# Round each type's range outward to whole powers of ten. Keep an axis span of at least one order of magnitude.
figure5_log_limits <- function(x) {
  log_range <- range(log10(x))
  lower <- floor(log_range[1])
  c(lower, max(lower + 1, ceiling(log_range[2])))
}
figure5_mass_log_range <- figure5_log_limits(mass_conditions$Concentration_std)
figure5_count_log_range <- figure5_log_limits(count_conditions$Concentration_std)

# Use mg/L directly for mass concentration. The plot coordinate for number concentration N follows:
# log10(Plot_y) = a * log10(N) + b.
# a and b align the endpoints of the two log10 axes; they are not unit-conversion factors. Equal heights do not mean equal concentrations.
figure5_axis_a <- diff(figure5_mass_log_range) / diff(figure5_count_log_range)
figure5_axis_b <- figure5_mass_log_range[1] - figure5_axis_a * figure5_count_log_range[1]

figure5_scatter_data <- exposure_conditions |>
  mutate(
    Plot_y = if_else(
      Concentration_type == "Mass", Concentration_std,
      10^(figure5_axis_a * log10(Concentration_std) + figure5_axis_b)
    )
  )

cat("For plotting only: log10(Plot_y) = ", figure5_axis_a,
    " × log10(particles/L) + ", figure5_axis_b, "\n", sep = "")

# Show actual concentrations as powers of ten. Each axis retains its own original concentration unit.
figure5_log_labels <- function(x) parse(text = paste0("10^", round(log10(x))))

# 3. Single dual-axis scatter plot: horizontal jitter only, with a fixed seed for reproducibility -------------------
figure5_scatter <- ggplot(
  figure5_scatter_data,
  aes(Duration_bin, Plot_y, colour = Concentration_type, shape = Concentration_type)
) +
  geom_point(
    size = 2.7, alpha = 0.60,
    position = position_jitter(width = 0.16, height = 0, seed = 701)
  ) +
  scale_colour_manual(
    name = NULL, values = c(Mass = "#2B7BBA", Count = "#D97925"),
    breaks = c("Mass", "Count"), labels = c("Mass concentration", "Number concentration")
  ) +
  scale_shape_manual(
    name = NULL, values = c(Mass = 16, Count = 17),
    breaks = c("Mass", "Count"), labels = c("Mass concentration", "Number concentration")
  ) +
  scale_x_discrete(drop = FALSE) +
  scale_y_log10(
    name = "Mass concentration (mg/L)",
    limits = 10^figure5_mass_log_range,
    breaks = 10^seq(figure5_mass_log_range[1], figure5_mass_log_range[2]),
    labels = figure5_log_labels, minor_breaks = NULL,
    expand = expansion(mult = c(0.04, 0.04)),
    # The right axis uses a strictly monotonic inverse transformation to recover N: N = 10^((log10(Plot_y) - b) / a).
    # Orange points use the mapped plot coordinates. The original number-concentration unit remains particles/L.
    sec.axis = sec_axis(
      transform = ~ 10^((log10(.) - figure5_axis_b) / figure5_axis_a),
      name = "Number concentration (particles/L)",
      breaks = 10^seq(figure5_count_log_range[1], figure5_count_log_range[2]),
      labels = figure5_log_labels
    )
  ) +
  labs(
    x = "Exposure duration (days)",
    caption = "Dual axes are aligned for display; the units are not interconvertible."
  ) +
  guides(colour = guide_legend(override.aes = list(alpha = 1, size = 3))) +
  theme_classic(base_size = 11, base_family = "sans") +
  theme(
    axis.text.x = element_text(size = 10.5),
    axis.text.y.left = element_text(colour = "#2B7BBA"),
    axis.text.y.right = element_text(colour = "#D97925"),
    axis.title.y.left = element_text(colour = "#2B7BBA", margin = margin(r = 8)),
    axis.title.y.right = element_text(colour = "#D97925", margin = margin(l = 8)),
    axis.title.x = element_text(margin = margin(t = 8)),
    legend.position = "top", legend.text = element_text(size = 10.5),
    plot.caption = element_text(size = 9, hjust = 0, margin = margin(t = 10)),
    plot.margin = margin(8, 8, 8, 8)
  )

print(figure5_scatter)
```

```{r}

# 4. Export the dual-axis scatter plot ------------------------------------------------
ggsave(
  "outputs/Figure5_Exposure_concentration_duration.png", plot = figure5_scatter,
  width = 6.3, height = 5.5, units = "in", dpi = 300, bg = "white"
)
```

```{r}
    transmute(
      Response_category = category,
      Response = as.character(values),
      Response_subgroup = as.character(ind)
    )
}))

# List unmatched or multiply classified responses as issues and stop further counting.
figure6_unmatched <- figure6_source |>
  anti_join(figure6_lookup, by = c("Response_category", "Response")) |>
  distinct(Study_ID, Response_category, Response)
figure6_duplicates <- figure6_lookup |>
  count(Response, name = "Assignments") |>
  filter(Assignments > 1)

  print(figure6_unmatched, n = Inf, width = Inf)
  print(figure6_duplicates, n = Inf, width = Inf)

}

  stop("Some responses have no Study_ID. Check them first to avoid incorrect counts of independent studies.")
}

  left_join(figure6_lookup, by = c("Response_category", "Response")) |>
  arrange(match(Response_category, figure6_categories), Response_subgroup, Response, Study_ID)

  group_by(Response_category, Response_subgroup) |>
  summarise(
    Number_of_studies = n_distinct(Study_ID),
    Study_IDs = paste(sort(unique(Study_ID)), collapse = ", "),
    .groups = "drop"
  ) |>
  arrange(desc(Number_of_studies), match(Response_category, figure6_categories), Response_subgroup)

  Response_names_in_Excel = n_distinct(figure6_source$Response),
  Response_names_classified = n_distinct(figure6_mapping$Response),
  Subgroups = nrow(figure6_counts)
), width = Inf)
print(figure6_mapping, n = Inf, width = Inf)
print(figure6_counts, n = Inf, width = Inf)
if (nrow(figure6_counts) != 16) {
  stop("The current data do not form 16 subgroups. Check the mappings and counts above. No categories are automatically removed or invented.")
}

figure6_colours <- c(
  "Biomass and Growth" = "#4C8DAE",
  "Biochemical Composition" = "#58A99A",
  "Functional Processes" = "#D9A441",
  "Community Diversity" = "#9B83B0",
  "Other" = "#D78282"
)
```

```{r}
#| label: fig-figure6-response-coverage

figure6_plot_data <- figure6_counts
# The first level of a discrete Y-axis is at the bottom. Reverse the display levels to keep the original first item at the top.
# Change only the display order. Keep study counts and data row order unchanged.
figure6_plot_data$Response_subgroup <- factor(
  figure6_plot_data$Response_subgroup,
  levels = rev(figure6_plot_data$Response_subgroup)
)
figure6_plot_data$Response_category <- factor(

# Show full names horizontally. Allocate label space from the actual text width.

  ) +

  theme_classic(base_size = 15.5, base_family = "sans") +
  theme(
    # The figure is 7.8 inches wide. At 16 cm wide in Word, response labels are about 12.5 pt.
    axis.text.y = element_text(size = 15.5, angle = 0, hjust = 1,
                               colour = "black", margin = margin(r = 8)),
```

## 4. Meta-analysis

### Hedges' g effect-size calculation

```{r}
#| label: hedges-g-calculation

# 1. Read response comparisons and create a separate dataset for effect-size calculation -----------------------------
# Keep the original statistical fields and extraction notes for traceability.
effect_size_data <- readxl::read_excel(
  "../03_Extraction_Data/data table - thesis.xlsx",
  sheet = "Effect_size_data"
)

original_cols <- names(effect_size_data)
stat_cols <- c("C_mean", "C_SD", "C_n", "T_mean", "T_SD", "T_n")
id_cols <- c(
  "Study_ID", "Experiment_ID", "Control_Arm_ID",
  "Treatment_Arm_ID", "Response_reported"
)

meta_data <- effect_size_data |>
  filter(if_any(
    all_of(c(id_cols, stat_cols, "Note")),
    ~ !is.na(.x) & trimws(as.character(.x)) != ""
  )) |>
  distinct() |>
  mutate(
    Record_ID = row_number(),
    Note_text = trimws(coalesce(as.character(Note), "")),
    # S03 Chao1 statistics have been extracted. Ignore the requires digitisation flag during screening.
    # Keep the original Note. This exception applies only to Prokaryotic Chao1 richness in S03.
    Note_for_screening = if_else(
      Study_ID == "S03" & Response_reported == "Prokaryotic Chao1 richness",
      gsub("requires digiti[sz]ation", "", Note_text, ignore.case = TRUE),
      Note_text
    ),
    # Keep the original Mean, SD and n unchanged. Create separate numeric columns for calculation.
    across(
      all_of(stat_cols),
      ~ suppressWarnings(as.numeric(as.character(.x))),
      .names = "{.col}_num"
    )
  )


# 2. Apply response-level note screening and flag shared controls and approximate SDs ---------------------
# Apply the same group exclusion decision to all treatment comparisons within a study, experiment, response and time point.
exclude_pattern <- paste(
  "excluded from (the )?(primary )?meta[- ]analysis",
  "not (directly )?(eligible|suitable) for Hedges",
  "not (be )?meta[- ]analy[sz]able",
  "narrative synthesis only",
  sep = "|"
)

review_pattern <- paste(
  "may not (be )?meta[- ]analy[sz]able",
  "error[- ]?(bar[- ]?)?type (was )?not reported",
  "replicates cannot be distinguished",
  "independence (was |is )?unclear",
  "requires digiti[sz]ation",
  sep = "|"
)

meta_data <- meta_data |>
  group_by(Study_ID, Experiment_ID, Response_reported, Endpoint_day) |>
  mutate(
    Group_note = paste(unique(Note_text[nzchar(Note_text)]), collapse = " | "),
    Note_excluded = any(
      grepl(exclude_pattern, Note_for_screening, ignore.case = TRUE) &
        !grepl("may not", Note_for_screening, ignore.case = TRUE)
    ),
    Note_review = any(
      grepl(review_pattern, Note_for_screening, ignore.case = TRUE)
    )
  ) |>
  ungroup() |>
  # Use control IDs to identify controls reused by different treatments, whether or not Endpoint_day is filled in.
  # Shared_control = FALSE does not mean that effect sizes within the study are statistically independent.
  group_by(Study_ID, Experiment_ID, Control_Arm_ID) |>
  mutate(
    Shared_control = n_distinct(Treatment_Arm_ID, na.rm = TRUE) > 1
  ) |>
  ungroup() |>
  mutate(
    Control_cluster = paste(
      Study_ID, Experiment_ID, Control_Arm_ID, sep = "__"
    ),
    # Flag S01 records with SDs approximated from fitted-model 95% CIs for sensitivity analysis.
    # Keep Note, Group_note and original statistics. Do not fill in missing Endpoint_day values.
    Approximate_SD = Study_ID == "S01" & grepl(
      "SD approximated|fitted[- ]model|95%[[:space:]]*CI",
      Group_note, ignore.case = TRUE
    )
  )


# 3. Apply study exclusions and basic statistical requirements ----------------------------------
# Exclude all records from S06 and S18. This takes priority over numeric completeness and Note screening.
s06_reason <- paste(
  "Excluded from the primary meta-analysis because the independence and",
  "correspondence of the two reported control datasets could not be reliably",
  "verified. Retained for narrative synthesis."
)

meta_data <- meta_data |>
  mutate(
    # Endpoint_day is not a required identifier. Keep missing S01 times as they are.
    Missing_ID = if_any(
      all_of(id_cols),
      ~ is.na(.x) | trimws(as.character(.x)) == ""
    ),
    Mean_ok = if_all(c(C_mean_num, T_mean_num), is.finite),
    SD_ok = if_all(
      c(C_SD_num, T_SD_num),
      ~ is.finite(.x) & .x >= 0
    ),
    N_ok = if_all(
      c(C_n_num, T_n_num),
      ~ is.finite(.x) & .x >= 2 & .x == floor(.x)
    ),
    # An individual group's SD may be 0, but the pooled SD must be finite and positive.
    Pooled_SD = sqrt(if_else(
      SD_ok & N_ok,
      ((C_n_num - 1) * C_SD_num^2 +
         (T_n_num - 1) * T_SD_num^2) /
        (C_n_num + T_n_num - 2),
      NA_real_
    )),
    # Record the main exclusion reason when several issues occur together.
    Exclusion_reason = case_when(
      Study_ID == "S06" ~ s06_reason,
      Study_ID == "S18" ~ "Replicate independence unclear",
      Note_excluded ~ "Excluded by endpoint-level Note; see Group_note",
      Note_review ~ "Pending review of endpoint-level Note; see Group_note",
      Missing_ID ~ "Missing comparison identifiers or response name",
      !Mean_ok ~ "Missing, non-numeric or non-finite mean",
      !SD_ok ~ "Missing, non-numeric, non-finite or negative SD",
      !N_ok ~ "Missing or invalid n: both groups require integer n >= 2",
      !is.finite(Pooled_SD) | Pooled_SD <= 0 ~
        "Pooled SD is zero or non-finite",
      TRUE ~ NA_character_
    )
  )

meta_ready <- meta_data |>
  filter(is.na(Exclusion_reason))


# 4. Calculate Hedges' g: Treatment - Control --------------------------------
# Apply the small-sample bias correction to SMD. Use the LS estimator for sampling variance vi.
# yi > 0 means only that the treatment response is higher. It does not directly indicate an ecological benefit.
if (nrow(meta_ready) > 0) {
  calculated <- metafor::escalc(
    measure = "SMD",
    m1i = T_mean_num, sd1i = T_SD_num, n1i = T_n_num,
    m2i = C_mean_num, sd2i = C_SD_num, n2i = C_n_num,
    vtype = "LS",
    data = meta_ready
  ) |>
    as.data.frame() |>
    as_tibble()
} else {
  calculated <- meta_ready |>
    mutate(yi = NA_real_, vi = NA_real_)
}

calculation_failed <- calculated |>
  filter(!is.finite(yi) | !is.finite(vi) | vi <= 0) |>
  mutate(
    Exclusion_reason = "Non-finite effect size or invalid sampling variance"
  )

# SE and 95% CIs apply to individual effect sizes. Use the normal approximation for these intervals.
effect_size_calculated <- calculated |>
  filter(is.finite(yi), is.finite(vi), vi > 0) |>
  mutate(
    SE = sqrt(vi),
    CI_lower = yi - qnorm(0.975) * SE,
    CI_upper = yi + qnorm(0.975) * SE
  ) |>
  select(
    all_of(original_cols), Record_ID,
    Control_cluster, Shared_control, Approximate_SD, Group_note,
    yi, vi, SE, CI_lower, CI_upper
  )

effect_size_excluded <- bind_rows(
  filter(meta_data, !is.na(Exclusion_reason)),
  calculation_failed
) |>
  select(
    all_of(original_cols), Record_ID,
    Control_cluster, Shared_control, Approximate_SD, Group_note,
    Exclusion_reason
  )


# 5. Summarise effect sizes, independent studies and inclusion counts for the specified studies -----------------------
# Keep separate treatment comparisons. Count independent studies by Study_ID and do not combine response indicators.
study_check <- tibble(Study_ID = c("S01", "S03", "S06", "S18")) |>
  left_join(
    count(effect_size_calculated, Study_ID, name = "Included_records"),
    by = "Study_ID"
  ) |>
  left_join(
    count(effect_size_excluded, Study_ID, name = "Excluded_records"),
    by = "Study_ID"
  ) |>
  mutate(across(c(Included_records, Excluded_records), ~ coalesce(.x, 0L)))

effect_size_summary <- effect_size_calculated |>
  group_by(Response_category, Response_reported) |>
  summarise(
    Studies = n_distinct(Study_ID),
    Effect_sizes = n(),
    .groups = "drop"
  ) |>
  arrange(Response_category, desc(Studies), Response_reported)

cat(
  "Total calculated effect sizes:", nrow(effect_size_calculated),
  "\nIndependent studies included:", n_distinct(effect_size_calculated$Study_ID), "\n"
)
print(study_check, n = Inf, width = Inf)
print(effect_size_summary, n = Inf, width = Inf)


# 6. Export calculable and excluded records with original statistics and extraction notes --------------------
# Retain S06 and S18 records and their exclusion reasons for narrative synthesis.
write.csv(
  effect_size_calculated,
  "outputs/Effect_size_calculated.csv",
  row.names = FALSE, na = "", fileEncoding = "UTF-8"
)

write.csv(
  effect_size_excluded,
  "outputs/Effect_size_excluded.csv",
  row.names = FALSE, na = "", fileEncoding = "UTF-8"
)
```

### Figure 7 — Overall group effects

Estimate the category-average effect separately for each of the four response groups. Response categories come from Excel; yi and vi come from the calculated effect-size CSV. Check arm IDs and original statistics when joining the inputs.
Keep only the grazer-excluded response for S01 and exclude all records from S06 and S18. Do not include Other in the category models. A study can appear in more than one category, so category study counts are not mutually exclusive.

Response composition and counts based on actual model inputs are saved in `Figure7_response_composition.csv`. Model and heterogeneity results are saved in `Figure7_model_summary.csv`. The reference classification table is used only for comparison. It does not automatically change categories in the current Excel file.

Interpret the pooled effect as the average standardised numerical change in the measured indicators. A positive value does not always mean improvement. Content per unit biomass differs from total biomass. The signs of changes in element ratios and LDH do not indicate the same direction of functional change. S04/S05 use leaf-decomposer contexts. S01 retains the SD extraction method based on CIs. S16 retains the note about inconsistent units in the original paper.
The S05 Simpson definition (D, 1−D or 1/D) still needs verification. The analysis keeps the original numerical direction. The category mean therefore does not represent changes in the same direction for every diversity index. Community Diversity has only 4 independent studies and is interpreted as exploratory.
The primary analysis uses a cross-response working correlation of ρ=0.5. Sensitivity analyses use 0, 0.3, 0.7 and 0.9. type/rho represents cross-response working correlation. Arm IDs and sample sizes approximate correlation from shared groups. The three random-intercept levels describe true heterogeneity between studies, between responses within studies and between treatment comparisons. Their role differs from sampling covariance.
The analysis steps create model objects and statistical summaries. Separate export chunks use the fitted objects to draw the figures.

```{r}
#| label: figure7-overall-group-effects
# 1. Read response categories and calculated effect sizes ------------------------------------
library(readxl)
library(dplyr)
library(metafor)

figure7_groups <- c("Biomass and Growth", "Biochemical Composition",
  "Functional Processes", "Community Diversity")
figure7_keys <- c("Study_ID", "Experiment_ID", "Control_Arm_ID", "Treatment_Arm_ID",
  "Response_reported", "Endpoint_day")
figure7_stats <- c("C_mean", "C_SD", "C_n", "T_mean", "T_SD", "T_n")

figure7_source <- read_excel("../03_Extraction_Data/data table - thesis.xlsx",
  sheet = "Effect_size_data", range = cell_cols("A:R")) |>
  filter(!is.na(Study_ID), !is.na(Response_reported)) |>
  select(all_of(figure7_keys), Response_category, Response_unit, all_of(figure7_stats), Note) |>
  distinct()
figure7_effects <- read.csv("outputs/Effect_size_calculated.csv",
  stringsAsFactors = FALSE, check.names = FALSE, fileEncoding = "UTF-8-BOM") |>
  tibble::as_tibble() |>
  rename(Response_in_calculated_csv = Response_reported) |>
  mutate(Response_reported = if_else(
    Study_ID == "S03" & Response_in_calculated_csv ==
      "Chlorophyll-a content normalized to ash-free dry mass",
    "Chlorophyll-a content normalized to AFDM", Response_in_calculated_csv
  )) |>
  # Apply the study screening rules: exclude S06 and S18 and retain only grazer-excluded S01 responses.
  filter(!Study_ID %in% c("S06", "S18"),
    Study_ID != "S01" | Response_reported == "Biofilm growth rate - grazer excluded")

# Excel provides categories, names, units and notes. The CSV provides calculated yi and vi.
# Standardise the S03 name matches with the dictionary below and check statistics for the same arms during the join.
figure7_data <- figure7_effects |>
  select(-Response_category, -Response_unit, -Note) |>
  left_join(figure7_source, by = figure7_keys, suffix = c("", "_Excel"),
    relationship = "many-to-one")
if (anyNA(figure7_data$Response_category)) {
  stop("Effect sizes do not fully match the current Excel data. Check IDs, response names or sampling times. Do not silently remove rows.")
}
for (column in figure7_stats) {
  current <- suppressWarnings(as.numeric(figure7_data[[paste0(column, "_Excel")]]))
  if (any(!is.finite(current) |
      abs(current - figure7_data[[column]]) > 1e-8 * (1 + abs(current)))) {
    stop("The Excel statistics have changed. Update the effect-size CSV separately first. This section does not recalculate them automatically.")
  }
}
# Trigger an input-consistency check if an Excel comparison has complete statistics but no matching yi and vi.
figure7_new_comparisons <- figure7_source |>
  mutate(across(all_of(figure7_stats), ~ suppressWarnings(as.numeric(.x)))) |>
  filter(Response_category %in% figure7_groups, !Study_ID %in% c("S06", "S18"),
    Study_ID != "S01" | Response_reported == "Biofilm growth rate - grazer excluded",
    if_all(all_of(figure7_stats), is.finite), C_SD >= 0, T_SD >= 0,
    C_n >= 2, T_n >= 2, C_SD > 0 | T_SD > 0) |>
  anti_join(figure7_effects, by = figure7_keys)
if (nrow(figure7_new_comparisons)) {
  print(select(figure7_new_comparisons, all_of(figure7_keys)), n = Inf, width = Inf)
  stop("Some comparisons in Excel have complete statistics but still need effect-size calculation or an eligibility check. Update the effect-size table first.")
}

# Standardise names in a separate analysis column. Do not infer Total EPS by adding its components.
figure7_aliases <- c("AFDW" = "AFDM", "BG activity" = "β-glucosidase activity",
  "Beta-glucosidase (GLU)" = "β-glucosidase activity",
  "Beta-glucosidase activity" = "β-glucosidase activity",
  "Leucine aminopeptidase activity (LAPA)" = "Leucine aminopeptidase activity",
  "Leucine aminopeptidase (LAP)" = "Leucine aminopeptidase activity")
figure7_data <- figure7_data |>
  filter(Response_category %in% figure7_groups) |>
  mutate(
    Response_standard = coalesce(unname(figure7_aliases[Response_reported]), Response_reported),
    Response_standard = if_else(Study_ID %in% c("S16", "S21") &
      Response_reported %in% c("LDH", "LDH activity"),
      "Lactate dehydrogenase activity", Response_standard),
    Response_standard = if_else(Study_ID %in% c("S17", "S19") &
      Response_reported %in% c("BIOLOG Shannon–Wiener functional diversity", "Shannon–Wiener index"),
      "BIOLOG Shannon–Wiener functional diversity", Response_standard),
    Response_standard = if_else(Study_ID == "S19" & Response_reported == "Shannon evenness index",
      "BIOLOG Shannon evenness", Response_standard),
    # Retain original group IDs and check for Arm_ID conflicts across experiments within a study.
    Response_category = factor(Response_category, levels = figure7_groups)
  ) |>
  arrange(Response_category, Study_ID, Response_standard, Treatment_Arm_ID, Record_ID)
stopifnot(!anyDuplicated(figure7_data$Record_ID),
  all(is.finite(figure7_data$yi)), all(is.finite(figure7_data$vi) & figure7_data$vi > 0))

figure7_inventory <- figure7_data |>
  group_by(Response_category, Response_standard) |>
  summarise(Original_names = paste(sort(unique(Response_reported)), collapse = "; "),
    Studies = n_distinct(Study_ID), Effect_sizes = n(),
    Study_IDs = paste(sort(unique(Study_ID)), collapse = "; "), .groups = "drop")
figure7_counts <- figure7_data |>
  group_by(Response_category) |>
  summarise(Studies = n_distinct(Study_ID), Effect_sizes = n(),
    Responses = n_distinct(Response_standard), .groups = "drop")
print(figure7_inventory, n = Inf, width = Inf)
print(figure7_counts, n = Inf, width = Inf)

# Use the reference mapping to check classifications. Match S03 names in the same way as the existing input join.
figure7_reference <- read_excel("Response_category_4_groups_mapping.xlsx",
  sheet = "Response mapping") |>
  transmute(
    Response_standard = if_else(
      Response_standard == "Chlorophyll-a content normalized to ash-free dry mass",
      "Chlorophyll-a content normalized to AFDM", Response_standard),
    Reference_category = Response_Category_new, Classification_note
  )

# Stop modelling and retain records for review if notes mention exclusion or uncertain independence.
figure7_note_review <- figure7_data |>
  mutate(Screening_note = if_else(Study_ID == "S03" &
    Response_standard == "Prokaryotic Chao1 richness",
    gsub("requires digiti[sz]ation", "", coalesce(Note, ""), ignore.case = TRUE),
    coalesce(Note, ""))) |>
  filter(grepl("excluded|not (directly )?(meta[- ]analy[sz]able|suitable for Hedges)|narrative synthesis only|independence.*unclear|requires digiti[sz]ation",
    Screening_note, ignore.case = TRUE)) |>
  distinct(Study_ID, Experiment_ID, Response_reported, Note)
if (nrow(figure7_note_review)) {
  print(figure7_note_review, n = Inf, width = Inf)
  stop("Some included records have notes that need review. Complete the manual decisions first.")
}

# 2. Interpretation and correlation assumptions for pooling different indicators --------------------------------
# Estimate the average standardised numerical change across measured indicators in a category. Do not interpret all positive changes as ecological improvement.
# Changes in LDH, C:N/C:P/N:P, content per unit biomass and BIOLOG functional indices cannot directly be interpreted as health changes in the same direction.
# Simpson may be reported as D, 1−D or 1/D. Keep the original numerical direction in the analysis.
# Community Diversity has few independent studies. Interpret its category-average effect as exploratory.
figure7_pooling_confirmed <- TRUE   # Keep the original numerical direction of each eligible indicator.
figure7_rho_confirmed <- TRUE       # Use the following cross-response working correlations for the primary and sensitivity analyses.
figure7_rho_main <- 0.5
figure7_rho_sensitivity <- c(0, 0.3, 0.7, 0.9)
if (!figure7_pooling_confirmed || !figure7_rho_confirmed) {
  stop("The inventory has been printed. First confirm the interpretation across indicators and the correlation assumptions. Then run the model and plotting sections.")
}

# 3. Fit the four groups separately: shared arms, cross-response correlation and multilevel variation in true effects --------------
# type/rho in vcalc represents the working correlation between different responses measured on the same samples.
# ρ approximates the working correlation when covariances are unreported. It is not a correlation estimated from these data.
# Use arm IDs and sample sizes to approximate correlation from shared groups. Do not additionally assume that experiments are independent.
# The three random-intercept levels describe true-effect differences between studies, between responses within a study and between treatment comparisons, respectively.
# V describes sampling correlation; random effects describe true heterogeneity. A non-positive-definite V produces a failure record.
# Method reference: https://wviechtb.github.io/metafor/reference/vcalc.html
fit_figure7_group <- function(dat, rho) {
  warnings <- character()
  result <- tibble::tibble(Response_category = as.character(dat$Response_category[1]),
    Rho = rho, Studies = n_distinct(dat$Study_ID), Effect_sizes = nrow(dat),
    Hedges_g = NA_real_, CI_lower = NA_real_, CI_upper = NA_real_, p_value = NA_real_,
    Test_df = NA_real_, Sigma2_study = NA_real_, Sigma2_response = NA_real_,
    Sigma2_comparison = NA_real_, QE = NA_real_, QE_df = NA_integer_, QE_p_value = NA_real_,
    Optimizers_agree = FALSE, Boundary_estimate = NA, Pool_shown = FALSE,
    LogLik_difference = NA_real_, Max_variance_difference = NA_real_,
    Status = "Model not fitted", Diagnostics = "")
  if (result$Studies < 2) {
    result$Status <- "Insufficient independent studies"
    return(list(model = NULL, summary = result))
  }
  tryCatch({
    V <- metafor::vcalc(vi, cluster = Study_ID, type = Response_standard, rho = rho,
      grp1 = Treatment_Arm_ID, grp2 = Control_Arm_ID, w1 = T_n, w2 = C_n,
      data = dat, checkpd = TRUE, nearpd = FALSE)
    dimnames(V) <- rep(list(as.character(dat$Record_ID)), 2)
    stopifnot(isSymmetric(as.matrix(V)),
      all(abs(diag(V) - dat$vi) <= 1e-10 * dat$vi))
    invisible(chol(V))
    run_fit <- function(control) {
      withCallingHandlers(metafor::rma.mv(yi, V = V,
        random = ~ 1 | Study_ID/Response_standard/Record_ID, data = dat,
        method = "REML", test = "t", dfs = "contain", control = control),
        warning = function(w) {
          warnings <<- c(warnings, conditionMessage(w))
          invokeRestart("muffleWarning")
        })
    }
    model <- run_fit(list(optimizer = "nlminb", iter.max = 2000,
      eval.max = 4000, rel.tol = 1e-10))
    # If the optimizer cross-check fails, retain calculable values from the primary fit and clearly mark them as provisional.
    check <- tryCatch(run_fit(list(optimizer = "BFGS", maxit = 2000, reltol = 1e-10,
      sigma2.init = pmax(model$sigma2, 1e-6))), error = function(e) {
        warnings <<- c(warnings, paste("Optimizer check:", conditionMessage(e)))
        NULL
      })
    result$Hedges_g <- as.numeric(coef(model))
    result$CI_lower <- model$ci.lb
    result$CI_upper <- model$ci.ub
    result$p_value <- model$pval
    result$Test_df <- model$ddf[1]
    result$Sigma2_study <- model$sigma2[1]
    result$Sigma2_response <- model$sigma2[2]
    result$Sigma2_comparison <- model$sigma2[3]
    result$Boundary_estimate <- any(model$sigma2 < 1e-8)
    result$QE <- model$QE
    result$QE_df <- model$k - model$p
    result$QE_p_value <- model$QEp
    if (!is.null(check)) {
      result$LogLik_difference <- abs(as.numeric(logLik(model) - logLik(check)))
      result$Max_variance_difference <- max(abs(model$sigma2 - check$sigma2) /
        (1 + pmax(abs(model$sigma2), abs(check$sigma2))))
      result$Optimizers_agree <- isTRUE(result$LogLik_difference <= 1e-3 &&
        result$Max_variance_difference <= 1e-3 &&
        max(abs(c(coef(model), model$ci.lb, model$ci.ub) -
          c(coef(check), check$ci.lb, check$ci.ub))) <= 1e-3)
    }
    if (!result$Optimizers_agree) warnings <- c(warnings, "Optimizer agreement requires review")
    for (fit in list(model, check)) {
      if (!is.null(fit$opt.res$convergence) && fit$opt.res$convergence != 0) {
        warnings <- c(warnings, "Optimizer returned a nonzero convergence code")
      }
    }
    core_ok <- all(is.finite(c(result$Hedges_g, result$CI_lower, result$CI_upper,
      result$p_value, result$Test_df, model$sigma2))) && result$Test_df > 0 &&
      all(model$sigma2 >= 0) && result$CI_lower <= result$Hedges_g &&
      result$Hedges_g <= result$CI_upper
    if (!core_ok) warnings <- c(warnings, "Core inference incomplete or invalid")
    result$Pool_shown <- core_ok && result$Optimizers_agree && length(warnings) == 0L
    result$Status <- if (!result$Pool_shown) "Review required; estimates provisional" else
      if (result$Boundary_estimate) "Numerical checks passed; boundary variance" else
        "Numerical checks passed; exploratory category average"
    result$Diagnostics <- paste(unique(warnings), collapse = " | ")
    list(model = model, V = V, summary = result)
  }, error = function(e) {
    result$Status <- "V or primary model failed"
    result$Diagnostics <- paste(unique(c(warnings, conditionMessage(e))), collapse = " | ")
    list(model = NULL, summary = result)
  })
}
```

#### Category-level main models

```{r}
#| label: figure7-main-models
figure7_models <- setNames(lapply(figure7_groups, function(group) {
  fit_figure7_group(filter(figure7_data, Response_category == group), figure7_rho_main)
}), figure7_groups)
figure7_model_summary <- bind_rows(lapply(figure7_models, function(x) x$summary))
print(figure7_model_summary, n = Inf, width = Inf)
```

#### Response composition and model results

```{r}
#| label: figure7-composition-model-output
# Use the data saved in the models to identify the responses actually included. Check them record by record against the inputs read in this section.
# V represents sampling correlation. Random intercepts describe true heterogeneity between studies, between responses within studies and between comparisons.
figure7_result_check <- lapply(figure7_groups, function(group) {
  result <- figure7_models[[group]]
  fit <- result$model
  current <- filter(figure7_data, Response_category == group)
  dat <- if (is.null(fit)) current else fit$data
  check_cols <- c("Record_ID", figure7_keys, "Response_category", "Response_standard",
    figure7_stats, "Response_unit", "Note", "yi", "vi")
  input_matches <- isTRUE(all.equal(
    as.data.frame(select(dat, all_of(check_cols))),
    as.data.frame(select(current, all_of(check_cols))), check.attributes = FALSE
  ))

  # Identify shared controls by study, experiment, response, endpoint and control arm.
  controls <- dat |>
    group_by(Study_ID, Experiment_ID, Response_standard, Endpoint_day, Control_Arm_ID) |>
    summarise(Treatments = n_distinct(Treatment_Arm_ID), .groups = "drop")
  arm_conflicts <- bind_rows(
    transmute(dat, Study_ID, Experiment_ID, Arm_ID = Treatment_Arm_ID),
    transmute(dat, Study_ID, Experiment_ID, Arm_ID = Control_Arm_ID)
  ) |>
    distinct() |>
    count(Study_ID, Arm_ID) |>
    filter(n > 1)
  V_order_ok <- V_diagonal_ok <- V_model_ok <- V_shared_arms_ok <- NA
  if (!is.null(fit)) {
    V <- result$V
    V_order_ok <- identical(rownames(V), as.character(dat$Record_ID)) &&
      identical(colnames(V), as.character(dat$Record_ID))
    V_diagonal_ok <- all(abs(diag(V) - dat$vi) <= 1e-10 * dat$vi)
    V_model_ok <- isTRUE(all.equal(as.matrix(V), as.matrix(fit$V), check.attributes = FALSE))
    same_scope <- outer(dat$Study_ID, dat$Study_ID, "==")
    shared_arm <- same_scope & (
      outer(dat$Treatment_Arm_ID, dat$Treatment_Arm_ID, "==") |
      outer(dat$Control_Arm_ID, dat$Control_Arm_ID, "==") |
      outer(dat$Treatment_Arm_ID, dat$Control_Arm_ID, "==") |
      outer(dat$Control_Arm_ID, dat$Treatment_Arm_ID, "==")
    )
    # Use the original model's working correlation across responses. Check only the nonzero positions in V; do not replace V.
    same_response <- outer(dat$Response_standard, dat$Response_standard, "==")
    expected_nonzero <- shared_arm & (same_response | result$summary$Rho != 0)
    nonzero <- abs(V) > 1e-10 * sqrt(outer(dat$vi, dat$vi))
    V_shared_arms_ok <- all(nonzero[upper.tri(V)] == expected_nonzero[upper.tri(V)])
  }

  # Use NA when optimizer convergence codes were not saved. Report whether a model was returned separately from whether numerical diagnostics passed.
  convergence_code <- if (is.null(fit$opt.res$convergence)) NA_integer_ else
    as.integer(fit$opt.res$convergence)
  tab <- result$summary |>
    mutate(
      Primary_fit_returned = !is.null(fit), Primary_convergence_code = convergence_code,
      Converged = if (is.null(fit)) FALSE else if (is.na(convergence_code)) NA else convergence_code == 0L,
      Numerical_checks_passed = Pool_shown,
      Input_matches_current_data = input_matches,
      Counts_match_input = Studies == n_distinct(dat$Study_ID) & Effect_sizes == nrow(dat),
      Studies_with_multiple_effects = sum(table(dat$Study_ID) > 1),
      Shared_control_groups = sum(controls$Treatments > 1),
      Arm_ID_conflicts = nrow(arm_conflicts),
      V_order_matches = V_order_ok, V_diagonal_matches_vi = V_diagonal_ok,
      V_matches_fitted_model = V_model_ok, V_shared_arm_pattern_matches = V_shared_arms_ok
    )
  list(data = mutate(dat, Model_fitted = !is.null(fit)), summary = tab)
})
figure7_model_summary_output <- bind_rows(lapply(figure7_result_check, function(x) x$summary))
figure7_model_input <- bind_rows(lapply(figure7_result_check, function(x) x$data))
figure7_count_check <- figure7_model_summary_output |>
  select(Response_category, Studies, Effect_sizes, Input_matches_current_data, Counts_match_input) |>
  left_join(mutate(figure7_counts, Response_category = as.character(Response_category)),
    by = "Response_category", suffix = c("_model", "_current"))
print(figure7_count_check, n = Inf, width = Inf)
if (any(!figure7_count_check$Input_matches_current_data |
    !figure7_count_check$Counts_match_input |
    figure7_count_check$Studies_model != figure7_count_check$Studies_current |
    figure7_count_check$Effect_sizes_model != figure7_count_check$Effect_sizes_current)) {
  stop("Figure 7 models do not match the current inputs. Fit the current data with the existing models before exporting. Do not reuse old results.")
}

# Response uses the model's standardised names. Original_names keeps the original spelling. Count studies by unique Study_ID.
figure7_response_composition <- figure7_model_input |>
  group_by(Response_category, Response_standard) |>
  summarise(
    Study_IDs = paste(sort(unique(Study_ID)), collapse = "; "),
    Number_of_studies = n_distinct(Study_ID), Number_of_effect_sizes = n(),
    Original_names = paste(sort(unique(Response_reported)), collapse = "; "),
    Model_fitted = all(Model_fitted), .groups = "drop"
  ) |>
  rename(Response = Response_standard, Study_ID = Study_IDs) |>
  left_join(figure7_reference, by = c("Response" = "Response_standard"), relationship = "many-to-one") |>
  mutate(Category_matches_reference = as.character(Response_category) == Reference_category) |>
  arrange(match(as.character(Response_category), figure7_groups), Response)
print(figure7_response_composition, n = Inf, width = Inf)
print(filter(figure7_response_composition, is.na(Category_matches_reference) |
  !Category_matches_reference), n = Inf, width = Inf)

# QE, its degrees of freedom k−p and its P value come from each primary model. The three sigma² values correspond to the three random-intercept levels.
# Keep the primary-model results and diagnostics used in the forest plot. Do not substitute rho sensitivity results or calculate single-level I².
print(figure7_model_summary_output, n = Inf, width = Inf)
write.csv(figure7_response_composition, "outputs/Figure7_response_composition.csv",
  row.names = FALSE, na = "", fileEncoding = "UTF-8")
write.csv(figure7_model_summary_output, "outputs/Figure7_model_summary.csv",
  row.names = FALSE, na = "", fileEncoding = "UTF-8")
```

```{r}
# 4. Four-row summary forest plot: blue-green squares, grey CIs and a dashed zero line ------------------
# Draw the title icon with base graphics to represent biofilm attached to a substrate.
draw_figure7 <- function() {
  # Increase all text by 25% and keep the font-size hierarchy. Keep symbol and line sizes unchanged.
  font_scale <- 1.25
  old_par <- par(mar = c(2.0, 0.5, 0.5, 0.5), family = "sans", bg = "white", xpd = NA)
  on.exit(par(old_par))
  plot(NA, xlim = c(0, 1), ylim = c(-0.45, 6.3), xaxs = "i", yaxs = "i",
    axes = FALSE, ann = FALSE, bty = "n")
  text(0.105, 5.95, "Benthic biofilm", adj = 0, font = 2, cex = 1.4 * font_scale)
  angle <- seq(0, 2 * pi, length.out = 80)
  polygon(0.058 + 0.031 * cos(angle), 5.82 + 0.10 * sin(angle),
    col = "#BBC4C5", border = NA)
  segments(c(0.037, 0.050, 0.065, 0.079), 5.91,
    c(0.035, 0.054, 0.063, 0.082), c(6.12, 6.05, 6.15, 6.08),
    col = "#287E87", lwd = 2)
  points(c(0.035, 0.054, 0.063, 0.082), c(6.12, 6.05, 6.15, 6.08),
    pch = 16, col = "#287E87", cex = 0.6)

  text(0.025, 5.05, "Response category", adj = 0, font = 2, cex = 0.88 * font_scale)
  text(0.355, 5.05, "Studies", font = 2, cex = 0.88 * font_scale)
  text(0.445, 5.05, "Effect sizes", font = 2, cex = 0.88 * font_scale)
  text(0.895, 5.05, "Hedges' g [95% CI]", font = 2, cex = 0.88 * font_scale)
  segments(0.025, 4.65, 0.985, 4.65, col = "#999999")
  rows <- 4:1
  tab <- figure7_model_summary
  valid <- tab$Pool_shown & is.finite(tab$CI_lower) & is.finite(tab$CI_upper)
  ticks <- pretty(range(c(0, tab$CI_lower[valid], tab$CI_upper[valid])), n = 4)
  if (length(ticks) < 2 || diff(range(ticks)) == 0) ticks <- c(-1, 0, 1)
  limits <- range(ticks)
  xpos <- function(value) 0.53 + 0.25 * (value - limits[1]) / diff(limits)
  segments(xpos(0), 0.7, xpos(0), 4.35, col = "#8A8A8A", lty = 2)
  for (i in seq_along(figure7_groups)) {
    text(0.025, rows[i], figure7_groups[i], adj = 0, cex = 0.93 * font_scale)
    text(0.355, rows[i], tab$Studies[i], cex = 0.93 * font_scale)
    text(0.445, rows[i], tab$Effect_sizes[i], cex = 0.93 * font_scale)
    if (valid[i]) {
      segments(xpos(tab$CI_lower[i]), rows[i], xpos(tab$CI_upper[i]), rows[i],
        col = "#707070", lwd = 1.4)
      points(xpos(tab$Hedges_g[i]), rows[i], pch = 15, cex = 1.0, col = "#287E87")
      text(0.895, rows[i], sprintf("%.2f [%.2f, %.2f]", tab$Hedges_g[i],
        tab$CI_lower[i], tab$CI_upper[i]), cex = 0.86 * font_scale)
    } else text(0.895, rows[i], "Review required", cex = 0.82 * font_scale, col = "#666666")
  }
  axis(1, at = xpos(ticks), labels = format(ticks, trim = TRUE), pos = 0.45,
    tck = -0.02, mgp = c(1, 0.45, 0), cex.axis = 0.85 * font_scale)
  text(0.655, -0.16, "Hedges' g", cex = 0.95 * font_scale)
}
```
